correctness.rationale: Definitions and domain are explicit: all 1<=k<=n, adjacency means disjoint k-subsets, rank<=3 in pure graph language. The exact three-move vertex-transitive extension lemma is proved directly. For n<2k, n=2k and k=1, structure and minimum order are elementary. For k>=2,n>=2k+1, every distinct pair has all third-vertex adjacency patterns except the possibly absent common-neighbour cell; that cell exists iff n>=3k-|A∩B|. All intersections t in 1..k-1 occur. This yields exactly three connected noncomplete pair spectra, while eight displayed rank-three sentence profiles distinguish every table row. The maximum minimum Kneser representative is binom(7,3)=35, and all other rows have representatives of order <=15. The standalone program independently computes exact rank-three FO types for eight representatives and 33 sampled parameter pairs, and checks the sentence truth tables. Finite samples are corroboration; the universal argument is combinatorial. No unproved lemma is used.

originality.rationale: The complete eight-class partition for every integer n>=k>=1 in pure adjacency and equality was not stated or implied by the inspected literature. The known k=2 strongly regular/complement-Johnson special cases do not cover the k>=3 mixed-codegree regime or the global sharp 35-vertex bound. The 2012 Kneser-neighbourhood article proves independent-set bounds; the survey treats general Ehrenfeucht games and strongly regular cases; the later Hamiltonicity paper proves cycle existence, not rank-three theories. A 1979 odd-graph article was inaccessible in full and remains a material possible-overlap risk. Search failure alone is not treated as proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: Biggs 1979 full text was inaccessible, so no decisive claim about its complete contents is made.
Unindexed or inaccessible bounded-rank studies of Kneser/odd graphs might contain the same classification.

The strongly regular k=2 subcase and the Johnson-complement subcase may already be logical corollaries of more general published theorems; originality attaches to the complete all-parameter classification and mixed-codegree boundary, not those subcases.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification over the entire classical two-parameter Kneser family, not an arbitrary slice or a numerical recomputation. It gives an exact finite rank-three testing set of eight graphs with optimal maximal size 35, and sharply identifies how low-rank first-order logic detects triangles and failure of common-neighbour coverage while losing the underlying set-size parameter. The mixed class covers all sparse odd graphs from k>=3, a structurally distinctive infinite sequence. The k=2 boundary, disconnected cases, and k>=3 mixed regime are unified in a single reproducible theorem; no downstream application or stronger theorem is assumed.
